utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. Today is Monday, the 18th of September, 2006. I'd like to greet everyone in the courtroom. Good afternoon, Mr. Scott, all of you Defence counsel and the accused here in the courtroom and I'm very glad to see that the three accused who were not here last week are now in a position to be with us. I'm very pleased about it. Furthermore, the Trial Chamber will now deliver two oral rulings. I'm going to read them slowly for the interpreters to interpret. First, we have a decision regarding the admission of documents related to Witness BK. On the 29th of August in order to decide on the admission of document P 08346 under seal parked for identification purposes, the Pre-Trial Chamber had asked the Prosecution to provide the decision that accompanied the death certificate. The Prosecution provided the document under number P 09696 on the 5th of September. On it we have 162 names of people who died in the Prozor municipality. The Prosecution asked the Trial Chamber to admit Exhibit P 08436 under seal as well as the list of names of deceased persons. The Defence was asked what it had to say about it and opposed the admission. After hearing the parties, the Trial Chamber believes that documents P 08436 and P 09696 for number 51 on the list, we believe that this confirms the statement of the witness with respect to the death of his father. Therefore, the Trial Chamber admits under seal documents P 08436 and P 09696 but only with respect to number 51. Let me sum up. We've decided to admit Exhibit P 08436 and as for P 09696, we only admit the part of the exhibit that is listed under number 51. This was the first oral ruling. Second ruling related to the application of Ms. Alaburic related on the 14th of September 2006. On that date, Ms. Alaburic asked for an extension of time as provided for in Rule 73 to reserve the possibility of appealing the decision of the 7th of December, 2006 -- 7th of September, 2006 for a judicial notice of adjudicated facts. In support of her application, she stressed the fact that she needed the translation into English of the said decision before requesting, if necessary, a certification for appeal. The Trial Chamber would like to recall that Rule 73 C of the rules provides that decisions for certification should be filed within seven days of the challenged decision. The Judges see no reason to -- not to go by this ruling or by this disposition. French is one of the working languages of this Tribunal and this Trial Chamber is a French speaking Trial Chamber. Therefore, it is up to the parties to organise their teams by -- and taking this into account. You can always have assistants who can speak French. As a result, the Judges have decided to partly dismiss the application made by Ms. Alaburic. However, exceptionally the Judges have decided to grant an extension of time until tomorrow, Tuesday, 19th of September, 2006. Therefore, we'll grant you an extension of time until tomorrow. Let me just say that this decision by the Chamber is a 35-page decision, but what was important even if you can't read French, what was important for you is to know which facts had been admitted and the admitted facts are listed very clearly in the decision. Number 7, 8, 9, 14, 15. Therefore, even if you can't read French you can see item 7, 8, 9, 14, et cetera have been admitted, and that is enough to give an overview of the decision rendered by the Trial Chamber. Therefore, you now have until tomorrow. We've extended the time limit of seven days and we've extended it to tomorrow. Therefore, you will have plenty of time to consider what you will do. Personally speaking, I would like to add the following: Judicial notice is a procedure that always provides for the Defence the possibility of rejecting these judicial notice. It's not because we decide to take judicial notice of something that it is accepted forever. Through the cross-examination of a witness you can always challenge items that have been accepted through this process. Final point before we proceed I'd like to notify the parties of the following, this is something that we've received today through the electronic system. As you know, the Judges met last week and they amended the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, especially with regard to Rule 92 bis, and the Judges have already adopted Rule 92 ter and 92 quater. 92 ter has to do with admissions of written statements and depositions and Rule 92 quater relates to unavailable witnesses. Considering the new Rules now adopted and the aim of which is to gain time, both the Prosecution and the Defence will be a position -- in a position in due course to submit lists of witnesses that might be heard according to Rule 92 bis in its new version or under Rule 92 ter. Let me specify that Rule 92 ter also relates to testimony that can prove the acts or the behaviour of -- or the conduct of an accused. So this is something completely new. I would like to invite you to read these new provisions, to consider them very seriously and to adapt your strategy in accordance to these new Rules. Today we have the last day of cross-examination of the witness we all know. If everything goes according to plan, we should be able to complete the testimony today, but if Mr. Karnavas was to find it necessary to prolong his cross-examination, he would be in a position to do so at the beginning of tomorrow's hearing in the afternoon. But knowing Mr. Karnavas and the way he can summarise his cross-examination, I'm sure he will be able to complete cross-examination today. I will now therefore ask the usher to bring the witness in. The witness has been waiting for several days to come back to this courtroom. I'd like to thank the counsel who gave us the documents they want to tender later on with the corresponding numbers. This will enable us to follow the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From what I understand, Mr. Pusic's counsel need an additional 15 minutes. Ms. Nozica will take 20 minutes, and then Mr. Karnavas will take the remainder of the time. Yes, Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have no further questions for this witness. We have completed our examination, and I informed the Defence of Mr. Prlic that if they wished to do so, they can avail themselves of our time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Ibrisimovic. I understand that you do not wish to put further questions to this witness. You've completed your cross-examination. Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. With the Court's indulgence I would like my colleague Mr. Karnavas to begin his cross-examination first because I think that it is proper that somebody who has not questioned the witness at all can could so first and I retain my right to my 20 minutes later on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. It's all the same to me. Mr. Karnavas, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take over the past week, you did not watch the proceedings when Mr. Galbraith was here?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just to be on the safe side, I have to ask you this question, I take it you did not go into the system check your transcript to see how he testified?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. Before I start, I just want to try to pin you down a little bit as to what exactly you are an expert in. You told us what you're not an expert in, the fields of the various disciplines that you have not studied. Could you please tell us, just very concisely for this particular case what is that you are an expert in? Can you describe it?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First I should make the distinction as a legal term and expert simply as somebody who knows quite a bit about a subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm asking you very concrete questions. What are you an expert in for this case? Don't tell me what in legal terms you are, because you're not a lawyer, you're not competent to give advice on that. So tell us, what are you an expert in?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've spent the better part of the last seven and a half years working with documentary evidence concerning, amongst other things, these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: These questions being the HVO, the HZ HB, that's it?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- well, among other things, the political and governmental structures and processes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So that's what you are an expert in?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And would that presuppose that you also looked into documents as to, for instance, foundational documents such as the constitutions?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which constitutions do you have in mind, because Herceg-Bosna did not have a constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I know it didn't a constitution, but Herceg-Bosna was in Bosnia- Herzegovina was it not?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now did you look at that constitution for that country?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've looked at the 1974 Bosnia-Herzegovina constitution but not for this particular report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Were you told not?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No I was not told not to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay now you told us that you had been given your marching orders, as they were, from the Prosecutor as to what you should do, what kind of a report you should you should prepare and I take it from listening to your testimony Mr. Scott left it up to you as the quote unquote expert what to look at and what not to look at?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well as far as --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not a questions I can answer yes or no because there's a number of premises in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well let me break it down, sir.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did Mr. Scott tell you what you do look at and what you could not look?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So it was your discretion.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he give you a page limitation?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He strongly suggested that I keep it under 100 pages, although I was not able to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask you to slow down. The interpreters find it difficult to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So keep it down to 100 pages?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, hold on. I was about halfway through the answer. I was told that I should keep it as brief as possible. It would be best to have it under a hundred pages although I wasn't able to do that. But I did get close but that was set as sort of a loose guideline for what it probably should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But if you needed 200 pages he wasn't going to stop you, was he?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And did he, in asking you to prepare this report, did he ask you just to prepare sort of an outline for the Trial Chamber to assist the Trial Chamber on what it is that this HZ HB was all about or did he also tell you to include any opinions, suppositions or what have you that you would come up with during in writing this report?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all I was told to avoid opinions and suppositions or anything that wasn't actually in the documents I was citing. As far as the first half of your question is concerned, I was told to give the Judges a very basic description of what these structures and organs were and processes were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right did you avoid providing opinions?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personal opinions that aren't based directly on the documents I cited, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Personal opinions. That means opinions that you hold yourself.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that I can't --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- base on the evidence which I'm using in this report yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Let me get ahead of myself a little bit. You called this a statelet the HZ HB at one point, that they created a statelet and you also called it a para-state. Now help me out here is that a conclusion or opinion: Yes, no, maybe, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, it's a term --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a term.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, just answer my question. You're Ph.D. from Yale, you've taken orals, you know exactly how to answer questions. So let's cut to the chase. Is that an opinion; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a characterisation but and it's a term that I chose to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is it an opinion?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that depends on what you call an opinion and that's a semantic question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if it walks like a duck, looks like a duck, swims like a duck, has feathers like a duck, quacks like a duck, is it not a duck?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this case, yes, it would be a duck.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay what was your definition by the way of what a state is before we can get to what a statelet is?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: A state as a -- that is number of things a state usually has.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is that based on your opinion or is that based on some knowledge are you going cite something?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't cite anything because I wasn't asked to I know in some other trials constitution experts --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is that based on some knowledge of yours, particular knowledge, did you look up what defines a state? I mean did you Google it for instance? Or is this something that you as a layperson, like the rest of us, are opining at this particular moment?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can explain if I go backwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just tell me one of the two. Did you have a definition of what a state is in front of you and if so, what was the basis of it? What did you look at? Did you constitution a constitutional scholar? Did you look at any books?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did no. The only thing I consulted in using the terms statelet and para-state in this stays is my own prior knowledge from history and from having worked here about the sorts of things people generally attribute to a state.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't asked to make constitutional conclusions about constitutional issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. You --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You would agree with me would you not and let's slow down a little bit I'm trying to compress about four days of cross-examination, but you would agree with me would you not that that's a term of art?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That which is a term of art, statelet?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or state?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be but it --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it doesn't necessarily have to be used as one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But in this instance, sir, you're using it as one, are you not?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you why I used it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not asking you why. I don't want why. When I want why, I'll ask why. In this instance, you are using it as a term of art, are you not? If you don't want to say yes or no just say maybe and move on?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that depends on what you call a term art. I think you could call anything a term of art if it's used -- it's more how the word is used rather than the word itself which would make it that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In this instance, sir, are you not using it as a term of art statelet and para-state are you not using that and there's a point to this?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hmm. Well, I'm not sure if saying term of art in this case has a particular legal meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll take that. I'll take that. You were asked a question last time by Judge Trechsel if I believe whether you were told specifically what to put in your report; do you recall that question?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The question being posed and you said no, he told you, you know, he left you free reign, didn't tell you what to do; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't put it like that my answer and I don't think I did then either. I was given a definition of the sorts of things I should be talking about and the sorts of things I should leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But he didn't tell you what to put in, that's what we're trying to get at. Mr. Scott didn't order you to put something into your report?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, no, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now and it struck me that that question was asked and we should take you at your bona fides but you know I'm a little troubled by that and I'll tell you why. You were commissioned to write this report in November 1993 -- 2005; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you had been working on this case for six years or cases related to this case for about six years prior to that right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, well over. You were familiar with the facts in this case; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Had participated in interviews?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, three I believe for this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. You had participated in strategy sessions?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it you were well aware of what the Prosecution's theory of the case was because you also participated to one degree or other in shaping the form of the indictment; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the first half of that, I was certainly aware of the general Prosecution theory of the case when you get down to the particulars of say the crime base that I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not talking about crime base.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- fuzzy about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're getting back to that statelet issue?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: General, okay well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That was part this strategy was it not or did that come to you out of blue to just call it statelet, didn't know anything about the Prosecution's case?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did know about the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although that's not why I chose terms I chose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, but you knew that was part of their theory and by the way there's no need to read the transcript. You understand English so you could just follow along and answer.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the last question about following along.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You don't understand my English you need to read it as well? I'm from the mid-west too, by the way, so we have the same accent more or less.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said earlier that I did --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right let's move on. Now, in the middle of writing your report, the Prosecution was preparing to amend the indictment; right? And in fact amended the indictment.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You don't know that the indictment was amended?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me think back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour the record will show the indictment the motion to amend the indictment was filed far before the report was prepared. It's a matter of record in the file.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I'll take that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So when you sat down to write your report, did you read the indictment by any chance?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But you knew what was in it?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you knew that the -- that the Prosecutor who is sitting right there was alleging that Herceg-Bosna, the HZ HB, or HR HB, was a para-state or a statelet?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to work backwards. Tell us, sir, in your opinion, what was functioning in the state of BiH as state?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. It falls outside of the scope of the report. The witness was not asked to do any work on the existing State of Bosnia-Herzegovina. He was asked to specifically give a report on the structures and functions of HVO and Herceg-Bosna. No part of his report was intended or commissioned to deal with the BiH government.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may respond, Your Honour, and I will deal with it as the Third Reich defence, he was only following orders. The point of this is as follows: How can you characterise something to be a statelet or a para-state within a state? How can you claim that you are objective and in his direct examination he said background in context, and the whole purpose of this is to show that the gentleman, and I dare say we will see, was totally ignorant of the state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, you have heard Mr. Scott. Could you answer him now with respect to the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Mr. Scott was on his feet, made an objection, said that didn't come within the scope of your expert report. Are you able to answer the question? Because after all you're somebody who has done important studies and you're an expert. You're qualified as an expert. So does your level of knowledge allow you to answer the question that Mr. Karnavas asked? And of course your answer will be useful to the Judges because everything that you say and that is said in the courtroom is of use to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I'll deal -- I think Mr. Karnavas asked a couple of questions and I can answer both of them based on my knowledge from working on other cases not based on what I looked at for this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So it's not in your report. There's nothing in your report about the state instruments, or whether the state was functioning or not from which then we can look and see how this para-state or statelet evolved; correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. And I wasn't asked to look into the Bosnia- Herzegovinian government.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm asking you a concrete question, sir. It's not in your report; right? Is the answer to that yes?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the answer was no, it's not in, and I've already answered that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's not in your report. Now, tell us what was functioning in BiH at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina organs, first of all, you have to make a distinction between what's functioning and what's functioning well and what's functioning in different places.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay let me walk you through.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was the central bank functioning sir: Yes, no, maybe, I don't know?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour again I'm sorry to interrupt but I'm going to make the point again I'm going to continue making the point. Mr. Tomljanovich is now speculating beyond the basis of his report and answering questions for which he's not prepared. He's not done any research to answer a questions as to whether the central bank is functioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's my point, they presented a report with a --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers not speak at the same time, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Witness, you have just said that you are capable of answering what was functioning and what wasn't functioning, that you could give an answer about that and it would be important for us to know what was functioning and what was not functioning. So tell us, please, what was functioning in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the State of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that is very broad -- I mean my knowledge on this have I'm speaking very broad and in very vague terms. First of all, I know the republican organs, they had police authorities and military -- which functioned with varying degrees of success all over the territory which they were able to control or had aspirations or -- to control. Now, as far as the central bank is concerned, that's something I don't know a lot specifically and of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know anything?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wait. If I may answer the question. As far as the central bank is concerned, the reason I didn't answer that is because I'm aware of the fact that the Prosecution calls on --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not asking you --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- asking the financial --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again -- excuse me, sir. Mr. President I'm going to object to this. Give me three or four days if he continues in this direction. I'm tired of this notchy defence, I'm only following orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I object to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was the central bank functioning? He either knows or doesn't know. Why is that important? It's important on the issue of whether in other areas of the country, the municipalities had to fend them in trying to develop some sort of payment system. That's why it's important. So when he's characterising it as a statelet, there must be some reasons and we need to get to the bottom of it. To what extent was the state functioning?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've understood the point. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Number one, the structure that Mr. Karnavas is trying to present a completely false and artificial one. Mr. Karnavas wants to make a point. It's a point that he's made in the proceedings before. It's point that I assume he'll continue to make and he may try to make in his own case to make his argument to present his case as to why Herceg-Bosna did what it did. But this witness is not prepared to address those matters, and I'm saying as a matter for the Prosecution Mr. Tomljanovich should not speculate and go outside the basis of his report. It's just like having anyone walk in here and start talking about any topic off the top of their head. This was not the purpose for which this witness was called, and it is not it's completely unfair for Mr. Karnavas to say that that somehow goes to the nature of his report. What he was asked to give a report about was the structure and processes of the HVO Herceg-Bosna, and whether any other government in Bosnia was functioning at the time is entirely beside the point. And finally before I sit down, Your Honour, I object in the strongest terms, and Mr. Karnavas should know better referring to me or anything that I do or my team says as Nazi-like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I object to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That was taken out of context. I said the Defence, I'm only following orders. We've heard this 20 minutes this is the Third Reich defence but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But if I may if I may very simply respond to the Prosecutor. Had the gentleman simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, are you not perhaps mixing things up? This is a witness, an expert. It's not an accused. He's not an accused so I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He's an employee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: -- your comparison on your Third Reich defence is really out of place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour I think -- I think -- I think -- I think, Your Honour, we've heard enough and every time the gentleman doesn't want to answer a question is: It's outside my scope. Now if you look at this report, if the report did not have opinions and only stated what was in the legislation, I wouldn't have a problem but the moment he's calling it a statelet, the moment he's calling it a para-state, it's opinion it's a conclusion and at that point in time, I'm entitled and the door has been opened for me to question him. He would have you believe and the Prosecutor would have you believe that this is an objective report, and I dare say it's not. Now, I'm perfectly willing to sit down and not ask any more questions if there is a finding of fact and conclusion of law at this point in time that one, he is biased. That two, that his report is not credible and that none of his testimony will be taken into consideration. But I think all of these questions are relevant. How can he formulate certain opinions if you don't look at everything in the historical context, in the background, and that's why I'm getting into it. They would have us believe that that the financial system that was put into place by Herceg-Bosna was somehow -- the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're not going to spend all our time discussing Mr. Scott's objection and Mr. Karnavas's responses. I'm going to put the question in the proper manner. Article 90 of the Rules is very precise. It is 90 H (ii) and this is what the Rule says it said if a party - "In the cross-examination of a witness who is able to give evidence relevant to the case for the cross-examining party," and Mr. Karnavas has the idea in his behind of showing that the Republic of Herceg-Bosna was the only state which showed that this -- which was functioning, and the party he is confronting the witness with the elements that the witness has and counsel should put that the witness the nature of the case to the party for whom that counsel appears which is in contradiction of the evidence given by the witness. So Mr. Karnavas is asking about the descriptions given by Herceg- Bosna but he wishes to talk about Bosnia-Herzegovina and how that functioned and he's just asked a question about the central bank. I would like to say that we did raise the subject of the central bank here in the court. It was a subject that we discussed. Now, at this point the witness can either answer or not. He can say yes, no, maybe. So it's up to the witness to answer, and that will be much more useful than to spend our time raising objections which slow down -- slows down the process. The Judges can see whether the witness is apt or inept in answering questions. If he has knowledge about the function of the central bank he will tell us. If not, he will also tell us. And if he researched the structure of the HVO and of Herceg-Bosna as a republic, he must have asked himself about -- questions about the functioning of the international monetary fund and the central bank and the relationships thereof, the dinar, the convertibility of the dinar and so on and so forth. So he's able to answer or not. Mr. Karnavas, please proceed but I'd like to remind you that you will have to look at the -- what the witness has said and the evidence you have and try to see if it tallies or if it does not tally. I think we have understood each other now please proceed and I'd like to appeal to both parties to remain calm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me back up. Go step-by-step. In your report, do you not fail to explain the cause and effect relations between the wartime events and the activities of all the conflicting parties?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the risk of being compared to the Nazis, I'll say that I didn't think that that was something that I was supposed to do so I didn't do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, concerning your methodology, accepting that you have told us what your task was from the Prosecutor and we've heard this many, many times, is it your understanding -- is it still your understanding that your report is objective and balanced? Yes, no, maybe?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. And I should also add that I didn't intend to put an entire case forward or comment on the entire case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You've told us that you've told us that and I don't need that tagline we've heard it. We've heard your excuses. Now, does -- does your report does it not lack context by simply focusing on the HVO while ignoring the actions of others and how they affected the Croats especially the Serbs, the Muslims the UN, the EC mediators and what have you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's an awful lot of things I had to ignore in order to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- be able to write a report which could be presented in one week.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is exactly what I'm talking about Mr. President I mean we're going to hear this excuse over and over again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Does it not lack context? Do you simply not focus on the HVO as if nothing else existed around the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Object to the form of the question. What was happening somewhere else has nothing to do with the structure of the HVO and whether the structure of the HVO whether the president was in the executive branch or in the HVO HZ HB or whether the exchange for services reported to the president or not. What was happening in Sarajevo has nothing to do with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour I'll move --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, Mr. Karnavas. I understood it that if an expert was given the task of investigating a subject then he studies the question but also looks at what's happening at the outside, around it, because an expert report must be a comprehensive report and not just on one aspect. That is how experts work. Then look at the whole picture. Take an example. If an expert in tropical medicine, for example, if he studies the effects of mosquito bites in Africa, he will have to ask himself about mosquito bites in Latin America. Proceed, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are you not selectively citing in your report that is what certain citations particularly the presidential transcripts?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're putting words in my mouth if I have to say yes or no on this question. I believe -- can I answer in one sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are you selectively not using portions of the transcript. You can say yes or no if you don't think you're doing that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have selectively using portions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And don't you think that by doing so you are providing a distorted interpretation of the citations that you're selecting?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not because --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Even if they're not in context?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- may I finish answering the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No. Do you not see the -- do you not see that perhaps you're putting something -- taking something out of context by just selectively choosing something out of a hundred page presidential transcript.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not because I know what I'm putting in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Well, at one point -- I don't want to get too far ahead of myself, but at one point you do mention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A follow-up question first. Mr. Karnavas, you've asked a question about presidential transcripts. Now, in your report when you quote a portion of the transcript I hope that you read the integral transcript, all of it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have, and on a number of occasions with the ones I cite those we've used on other cases and those I also indexed years ago so I've seen all of those quite frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now just as an example and I don't want to spend too much time at this point in time on it, but you do cite the presidential transcript of September 17, 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I did notice that not all pages of that presidential transcript were put in for translation. Is there a particular reason? In other words, what was translated was only the part that you or somebody at the OTP thought was necessary to have translated and not the entire portion?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can answer that question. That's mainly a problem of resources. Now, with the transcripts, we have in our possession right now well over 660 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, you've told us what the resources were.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But here you are citing a presidential transcript, 17 September 1992 and the pages that were omitted less than 50 and I'm referring to, for the record, P 00498. I'm curious who is the person or persons that select what portions of a transcript or what portions of a document especially one that I have cited will not get translated albeit it might contain some information that could be viewed as exculpatory for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the -- as this witness has already indicated and demonstrated in court repeatedly he reads and works in B/C/S. He writes -- he reads and works in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's not the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So whether it was translated or not doesn't have anything to do with what this witness has read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's precisely the question that I was going to ask. And thanks to the relevant question, pertinent question asked by Mr. Karnavas with respect to the transcript, 50 and 60 per cent of the pages were translated it's a problem of resources. Now, the question that arises is what about the pages not translated into English? Now you know B/C/S. Did you read them in B/C/S then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This particular transcript I've read repeatedly, yes, in B/C/S and the -- to answer Mr. Karnavas's question put earlier, it's persons like myself, various analysts who read the original who decide which passages get translated and which do not because we simply don't have the wherewithal to translate every single page of every single transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So it's you or someone like you who in this instance will decide what portions of a transcript that might contain exculpatory evidence will not be translated?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, no. That's not true. If there is exculpatory evidence then that's a Rule 68 issue then we have to translate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you obviously know what rule 68 material looks like, not being a lawyer, as you told us over and over again?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone who works in the OTP is briefed frequently on what is Rule 68 material and encouraged that if there's even a shadow of a doubt that something may be Rule 68 then it should be brought to the attention of the lawyers if you're not sure about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, just since we're on this topic on the 17th of September, if we were to look at this entire transcript, not just portions that you decided or somebody else decided to translate and just cite, but the entire context this conversation, first of all, I think we can agree that there are a lot of people participating in this meeting; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite a few, yeah, I'm not sure exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it would appear that everyone gets an opportunity voice their opinion?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure of that. Frequently in the transcripts, people who are present do not speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But there are lots --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- lots of folks are giving their opinion in this transcript; correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I think we can agree that the general essence of this conversation that's taking place deals with the Croatian question in Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the question of Herceg-Bosna and what to do with it. I don't know if I'd say call it the Croatian question necessarily but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, certainly --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You don't want to misrepresent to the Trial Chamber that the entire conversation has to do with Herceg-Bosna, do you? And I remind you you're under oath. Inside, they're talking about what to do and how to protect the Croatians in Bosnia and Herzegovina; are they not doing that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is false - we're on a false trail here. The entire transcripts have been known and turned over the Defence years ago. All the accused know B/C/S, most of the lawyers read B/C/S, so if there's a suggestion that there's been selective disclosure on what' translated or not translated, they have the entire -- every single entire transcript. They've had them for months if not years and they all read in B/C/S. If there is some other part of the transcripts they want to use, they can use it in their own case. They can put the specific question to the witness. We're just going down completely false trails here they're going down and wasting time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir was this not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You seem to be saying that in the expert report -- the expert report was only based on certain passages translated in English whereas there were B/C/S passages that would go to your case. So give us an example, put the pages to the witness, say: Why didn't you refer to such and such passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we're going to put in the entire document but when I have such time limitations which are, with all due respect, unrealistic to conduct the cross-examination of this kind of a witness, it's impossible. But I don't want you - well, you can shake your head all you want, Judge Trechsel, but it is. I can assure you. And if there is better way or faster way, I'd like to know it with you in this particular what I want to do is goat the essence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you haven't got an example to quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... give an example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Give us an example then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let's look at what Jozo Maric said, and it starts on page -- let me have a moment, Your Honour. Okay it would be 01508795. Now, the Prosecution stopped the translation on page -- on the previous page in the middle of what Jozo Maric was saying. While that's being pulled up, let me ask a couple of preliminary questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, do you know who Jozo Maric is?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was an HDZ politician I believe from Grude, and he was also in the commission for exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And incidentally this -- I guess the documents that we're referring to is 1D 00918, for the record. Now, in -- now, you said you read this several times. Do you recall by chance what Jozo Maric was -- was advocating at the time?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's look and see what was omitted. And this is on the page 01508795. He says in the middle of the page and I'll just read slowly: "I'm saying this first of all because of historical continuity. I'm interested in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Croatian people as a whole in the following hundred 200 or 500 years." The page I guess it would be 1D 33-0032. "If we agree now to a civil unitary Bosnia-Herzegovina, we will live to see what the municipalities in Central Bosnia saw in the last 30 or 40 years. So by having lenient attitude and by constant movement westwards, we are just going away, but if we have our areas in future, our municipalities, we will remain there, and we will invest more easily. We will have our schools, et cetera." And he -- the next passage talks about Livno. Now, if you go into the next page, in the middle of it with the paragraph it says: "Therefore, for the future of my grandchildren and those who would like to return, I want my piece of land. I want my share without giving up, without giving up," I point this out, "without giving up Bosnia-Herzegovina as a whole, and for what I am often criticised." Now, if that's something that should be included that's exculpatory, I don't know what is, but this page was not even included in their document and is certainly not cited by this gentleman, but I'll go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, we're not going to allow it to go on while Mr. Karnavas has mischaracterised the record. Number one, there's no indication of anything of how that's exculpatory of any of the accused. There's no indication whatsoever; in fact, it's consistent with the Prosecution's case. Third, we tendered the entire document into evidence, it is Exhibit P 00498. Now, what Mr. Karnavas is trying to suggest is that the Prosecution has selectively used this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: These pages --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We have tendered the entire transcript into evidence in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Not in English, Your Honour, not in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: For the reasons indicated and the counsel can do they can use any other part of this they wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So much for going for the truth. So much for taking the Prosecution at its bona fides.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's false, Your Honour, because the witness has testified several times now that he read the entire transcript in B/C/S himself. So everything that -- if Mr. Karnavas if he would think before he moves his mouth and what's been done and not been done, it would be much better for everyone, because the witness has said I reviewed the entire document in B/C/S. The entire document is in the record the Prosecution tendered the entire document we have kept nothing from the Court for the Defence so all these allegations and insinuations by Mr. Karnavas are just dead wrong and I object to it. This cannot be allowed to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now if we go on to the next page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, Mr. Karnavas. This is how I understand the situation: It appears that in the presidential transcript in B/C/S we saw Mr. Maric's intervention and he raised a point that was related to Bosnia-Herzegovina, and, I'm summarising now, it seems to say -- or, rather, on the Croatian side, the decisions will be taken up and implemented. They will be applied. Now, if it was translated into French, the Judges would have been able to understand the expert report better and to appreciate it better. Now, what Mr. Maric said, does it go against your vision, the vision you gained? What do you think? Yes or no? We can see you shaking your head, but would you like to explain, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can tell from the passage of Mr. Maric's speech which was read to me, that's exactly what the general thinking was, that they did not want -- the people involved in Herceg-Bosna at that time did not want to have a centrally organised Bosnian state, or as they usually would put it, a unitary Bosnia-Herzegovina. They wanted control over their own municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It says "Without giving up Bosnia-Herzegovina." They're not talking about breaking away. They're not talking about being annexed to Croatia. And now -- and he's -- and incidentally Tudjman is president at the time; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, you're saying, They're not talking about breaking away. I say, He's not talking about breaking away. Well, in -- although I'm sure what he says in that Croat because I said repeatedly and this is the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, I'm asking you -- I know you want to filibuster, but I'm asking you a different question. He says without giving up Bosnia- Herzegovina; is he not saying that? Can you not see that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me see. I wouldn't be surprised if he said that at this juncture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, later on in the following page, 0501508797, so that would be the following page, in the middle of that paragraph he says and I'll just read slowly: "I support what someone said we should return all able-bodied young men from Bosnia-Herzegovina who are bathing in the sea while walking around because they have the obligation to defend their homeland just like those who stayed there. They come here to work as waiters, to work at this and that, and find all possible ways." Now, here, sir, is Mr. Maric not saying that Croats from Bosnia- Herzegovina should get back to Bosnia and Herzegovina to defend their motherland? Is he not saying that here?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although -- and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll take the yes --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I should add that I think when he thinks of the motherland, he's thinking of Herceg-Bosna, not the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm saying. He's asking those people -- because there are allegations here that everybody that went to Croatia was this foreign force, and here we have Jozo Maric saying that Croats from Bosnia and Herzegovina who are either bathing at the sea or working as a waiters in wherever should get back to defend Bosnia and Herzegovina; right? That's what he's saying.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this first of all is consistent with what else I say in the report. The problem of people hiding in the Republic of Croatia not turning up for service is something that's mentioned quite a bit in my report and the meeting in October of 1993 is mentioned as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. Now, after that, and I don't want to spend too much time on this, Mr. President, because I do -- we all will have the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, just one point. You've just outlined the statement of Mr. Maric and based on this statement you've contradicted the statements of the witness, but under the guidelines set by the Chamber for the admission of exhibits, we stated what that -- that when a party wishes to challenge an exhibit, that party then has to submit the translation of the relevant document of the text, therefore the translation here of the statement of Mr. Maric, do you have this translation in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I thought it was provided. It's 1D -- 1 -- 1D 00918. We translated all the missing pages in English so you would have the entire transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And after that, we see that Mr. Zoran Buntic speaks. I don't want to go into it, but let me just say one thing regarding this. Would it be fair say, sir, that if we were to read this entire transcript and put it into context what we have is a dialogue among all sorts of folks trying to figure out how to resolve the Croatian question in Bosnia and Herzegovina? Isn't that what it's all about, the general essence of this discussion?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, once again I wouldn't necessarily phrase it saying the Croatian question in Bosnia and Herzegovina, because that implies certain things, but yes they're talking about the situation of Croats in Bosnia and Herzegovina. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And -- and the gist of this is nobody's asking for annexation to Croatia or for breaking away from Bosnia and Herzegovina, are they, if we - - if we look at this entire transcript, and the Judges will be able to read it.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I answer the question? Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I mean it would be nice if you could.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no one is proposing full independence at this juncture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now in -- I'm talking about in this -- we're talking about this conversation, sir. I'm not talking about some other juncture?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So work with me. Work with me. You know, we're talking about September 17, 1992. You know, it doesn't take a rocket scientist to figure this out. In this discussion here. They're not talking about breaking away, is it?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll try my best to work with you. What they're talking about, and if I could summarise the general gist of what's decided here --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, is anybody advocating at this point in time to break away, to form a statelet?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: To form a para-state? Is anybody saying it's a yes or no. The Judges will have the transcript. They'll make the determination

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, let the witness answer. If Mr. Karnavas is going to ask a question, then let the witness answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The counsel, based on the transcript of 17 September 1992, including Mr. Maric's statement starting at page 12 in the English version, therefore, the Defence is asking whether Mr. Maric talks about the possible dismantling of Bosnia and Herzegovina in favour of Herceg-Bosna or Croatia. The question is rather straightforward. What do you think about this matter? Because you've read the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or as Mr. Karnavas seems to be suggesting, they're saying exactly contrary. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, first of all, and maybe it's a problem with the translation, but I believe what Your Honour just asked me is slightly different than what Mr. Karnavas just asked me. If the question were simply what Mr. Maric thought, then I would say I don't remember the entirety of his speech. If the question is what everyone at the meeting was saying and doing and what the general consensus was, that's another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Answer the latter question. Are you suggesting that there was somebody in there advocating for the Croats to break away or break away from Bosnia-Herzegovina or dismantle Bosnia-Herzegovina? Yes, no, maybe, I don't recall? Four choices, pick one.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid if I can only pick those four choices I can't give you a very good answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, very well.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I can give you a two-sentence answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm just asking is there anything when we read this when we walk away will the Trial Chamber walk away with the impression that what is being discussed in here by anyone is that the Croats of Bosnia and Herzegovina are talking about dismantling the State of Bosnia-Herzegovina and going off on their own, creating a statelet or being annexed to Croatia? Yes, no, maybe?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're definitely talking about creating their own institutions and creating something that's -- I would call a statelet, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. What you would call a -- now, is that a term of art when you call if a statelet --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can go --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- yes or no? Is that a term of art because we need a definition there what is a statelet on based on what educational background you're going to give us this opinion? So is that a term of art yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, if it's a term of art or not I stated earlier that that's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Then we'll move on. Sir, we'll move on. To what extent was the central government able to pay salaries at the municipal level, at the local level? Do you know? If you don't know say I don't know. So I don't want you guessing?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure it was different in a lost different places.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm asking you yes or no, sir, were they able to pay salaries for the teachers? Were they able to pay for the medical facilities? Were they it able to pay for the pensions? Were they able to provide the normal and necessary services that state institutions who would be able --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- and are required to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to put the question to the witness myself to avoid any objections. Sir, you're an expert. The question that was put to you is the following was the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in a position to pay the teachers, because that's the example that's mentioned here, was it in a position to pay their salary? Do you know, you don't know, you can't answer? That's a straightforward question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just ask for clarification as to where and when to pay the teachers in Sarajevo in 1992 or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Outside Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- or Tuzla, or where? Where and when?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was it in a position -- were they in a position to pay the salaries in Sarajevo or in the -- on the entire territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Or maybe you've not looked at the issue. That's also another possibility here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I haven't looked in the issue. There are things I can say from my general impression but that's all I'm be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll accept that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but what's the general opinion? You've said that you've not looked into the matter but that you can give a sort of general impression, general opinion about this. What is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well -- yes, well I know generally, especially in the earlier periods of the war that persons not just in government but in general in quite a number of the former Yugoslav republics not just Bosnia and Herzegovina were paid infrequently if at all, and I would be very surprised if everyone were being paid and certainly be very surprised if they were all being paid on time, because I know that there wasn't the funds to pay people in general, especially in the early periods of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in preparing your report also as I understand it that you didn't think it was necessary to consider the peace proposals as they - - and how they relate, perhaps, to that period or time.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I department think it was appropriate because I thought that was going to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- dealt with by live witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My questions are very precise. If I want to know whether it was appropriate or not I'll ask you. The question is you did not consider it; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had to consider them as part of the broader context and I did, but the point of the report wasn't to reach any conclusions or even to give the Judges information about the peace --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- plans and piece negotiation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you say in the greater context in the general context, where in your report do you cite anything about the peace proposals and how perhaps a particular peace proposal that's on the table might be affecting what is going on on the ground? Is there anywhere in your report there?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I believe in at least two occasions I mention the Vance- Owen Plan --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in connection with the first half of 1993 because this is something which all of the persons active in Herceg-Bosna were talking about a great deal as was everyone in Bosnia at the time, and then I believe I mention Owen-Stoltenberg --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in the late summer --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- at least less than I mention the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In your report, do you do you not fail to examine critically the actions of the Muslim side and the workings and the legitimacy of the Bosnian government?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Outside the scope of the report Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We've heard that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm going keep saying it Mr. Karnavas with put questions to the witness for the next two weeks that have nothing to do with his report this witness was not asked to look at the Muslim side of the government. He was asked to look at the structures and processes of Herceg-Bosna and the HVO during the time period 1991 to 1994. He was not commissioned to do any work of --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We've heard this, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- do a report based upon what the Muslims were doing or not doing. It's outside his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We've heard this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to keep on saying it. I do not understand why it is so difficult for anyone in the courtroom to understand the concept what Mr. Tomljanovich was asked to do and what was in the scope of his report and what is outside the scope of his report. It's a very basic concept. It's stated in report itself I have quoted it to the Chamber of what the scope and what the purpose of the report, it's stated in the report, I won't quote it again. I don't know why it's so difficult for Mr. Karnavas to understand that concept.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott is right, Mr. Karnavas. If you put the question it's because you're relying on something or you want to establish something. What do you want to establish?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Here's why I objected because as I noted, another Trial Chamber would not accept such the gentleman as an expert but we have in this case because of the tradition we have in this Tribunal. The gentleman was asked to write a report about, you know, about how Herceg-Bosna was created and how it was established. It wasn't established in a vacuum. Things were going on. Things were happening. They were reacting. Their peace agreements, their friendship agreements all of these things are driving the process. So if -- and I keep stressing this, Mr. President and Your Honours, if the report was merely an account of what the legislation was, the dates and chronology, then I wouldn't be here doing this. But the moment that we have argument, the moment that we have opinion, the moment that he's forming conclusions especially when the gentleman tell us that he's ignorant of the various disciplines that would require them to form those opinions, at that point in time, it is my God- given right here as a Defence lawyer to be able to challenge him and to show that the report is biased, is one-sided. It's not -- they can't have it both ways. They've created the problem. If they -- if they want to excise all of the opinions, all the conclusions and then resubmit the report, then I -- I have no problem and I would be more than happy to assist them on that project. It might turn out to be like ten pages, but that's what we're talking about, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, not one thing that Mr. Karnavas has said so far contradicts the report of this witness. Everything he has asked him so far has been largely -- sorry I don't want to -- not everything, most of what has been asked by Mr. Karnavas has asked so far was been completely outside the scope of this report, and this witness' work, and nothing contradicts what he's done. Not one single thing in the last hour and a half two hours not one thing has contradicted this witness so it's just a false statement by Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: May I simply proceed, Your Honour? I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, let's just look at some of your report you will know we're not going to have a chance to look at all of it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ibrisimovic was on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. If I might be of assistance. I think that the witness did deal with the reactions from Sarajevo and some decisions of the Constitutional Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina as well. So what Mr. Karnavas is asking I think is in order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, and we're going to get to that constitutional decision, Mr. President, but I'll move on I just --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In your first paragraph, you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Sorry, there's something I failed to understand or probably misunderstand, I wouldn't like to stay with the misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I look at the report which ends with a sort of a summary, and if you look at the very large paragraph in 333, I read that the HZ HB was replaced by a new constitutional framework with the HR HB beginning in August 1993. The new HR HB was more permanent and more like a state than HZ HB had been. I read that as saying that it was not a state but less unlike a state than the previous was unlike a state. And whereas, of course, the terms like statelet and things like that come up, I think that this is the essence of the report, and I think that it is a bit of a skeet shooting to go at single occurrences where the terms like state or statelet come up when we have a statement here that I read as being quite nuance and open to the issue which obviously is contested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would agree with you in part. Again, I cannot overstress that I need three or four days to cross-examine this individual. It would be calm. It would go step-by-step. I don't have that luxury. So when you're saying skeet shooting. I'm trying to shotgun this approach. I don't particularly enjoy this. I can tell you I have over a hundred hours of preparation in this for this three-hour preparation. It's not fair, but this is the best that we can do. So if I may -- if I might go on, hopefully I'll clear things up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In your report on paragraph 1, you say you focus on the top "on top levels of government in administration." You say that. But you do not examine whether the top levels were able to effectively control local units or extra governmental groups and organisations. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's two questions there. First of all, as far as local governments is concerned, I do address that as best I can with what the documentation allows me to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, sir.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as extra.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
