utterances.text: Well, there is a lot of premises in this question. I'm not sure Akmadzic was acting within his power but this is outside of the scope I intended to talk about and like I said, if you want to know why --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are you suggesting, sir, that these documents and we can talk in open court, are you suggesting that these documents, the one that I have shown to you are somehow forged?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I'm suggesting at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Oh, okay. So if it is not an Official Gazette, would it not be available to the public?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So someone like Izetbegovic or his associates, his close associates, others involved in the government and received the Official Gazette, they would have been able to see this; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you're not suggesting that Akmadzic somehow just slipped a Mickey into the Official Gazette as it were, and you know what I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. But whether he was act being outside of his powers or not and whether or not there was a reaction to that, and that's just one part of this whole thing, on whether or not that's the question, I don't think they ever solved within the authorities there because Akmadzic didn't remain at that post much longer after this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And are you suggesting that that's why he got fired? Is that the implication?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believe Mr. Akmadzic left on his own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But you have no evidence whatsoever to challenge the authenticity or the intent behind this decision, do you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it you haven't read the law on state administration as well. I mean, if you haven't -- right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which law on state administration? BiH law on administration?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who are we talking about? BiH. Work with me, at least within the geographical scope.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's precisely the problem there's more than one set of laws in the geographical area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There's the state law the law of state administration it's pretty complex by the way?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen it but I did not review it for this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. I don't know how I'm doing on time, Mr. President. I'm kind of -- if I could be told when we have our break so I could just guesstimate how far to go or where to go next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We could take the break now, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It could be good. I could organise myself and then -- I can't promise I'll be able to finish tonight but I'm doing my level best as you can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. We're counting on you. It's 5.20 now. We'll take a 20-minute break and reconvene at approximately 20 it 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Karnavas, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, in light of the circumstances and in light of what was happening in -- in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time that the -- that the Croats organised themselves, the Croats of Bosnia-Herzegovina, do you think it was unreasonable for them to organise in anticipation of similar occurrences of what was happening in Croatia, for instance?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the broad sense of organisation, no, although specifically doing what they did is another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And you have an opinion on that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: A personal opinion but one which I tried to keep out of the reports as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, would not the -- I mean, I take it you must have heard what happened in Ravno.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you say many times in the sense that you've heard it from people or you actually know what happened?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, every case I've worked on, the Defence brings it up a few times, every HVO-related case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You say the Defence brings it up as if it's some kind of dirty thing. I guess what I'm trying to get at is what happened in Ravno; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Beyond the scope of the report, Your Honour, and also I object to Mr. Karnavas's characterisation. The witness never said anything about bringing it up as if it's a dirty thing. That is purely, once again, Mr. Karnavas's commentary, and again I go back to this is beyond the scope of the report. It has nothing to do with Ravno.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, and I guess --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, what is the point and the relevance of Ravno? In what way can this be useful for your case?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The gentleman was asked to write a report of the establishment of HZ HB. One might ask why was it established how was it established, under what time was it established, what were the circumstances? The gentleman indicated that he had a personal opinion about what -- what the Croats did, and I think if I'm allowed to proceed, we will see that we're in the living in an Alice in Wonderland world here. There are real events taking place and the HZ HB is established when real events are taking place however much we want to say others are going to discuss it, he's an expert and I'm merely asking him concretely. And the gentleman did go out of his way to say that the Defence bring it up all the time, and I thought the tone and the manner in which he said that seems to indicate that it's as if -- you know, to minimise the events in Ravno.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The fundamental false premise of much of Mr. Karnavas's comments just now and throughout the cross-examination is just made clear again at lines 15 and 16 of Mr. Karnavas's statement. "The gentleman was not," and I repeat not "asked to write a report on the establishment of the HZ HB. He was asked to write a report on the structures and -- governmental structures and processes of the HZ HB." Whether they were good or bad, what their historical reasons were. This is -- they had the president, they had a cabinet. They had a legislature called the Presidency. They had a military, a Ministry of Defence. They were related to the military this way. He was never asked to write a report on the history on the establishment of Herceg-Bosna and whether it was justified or not. And that is the whole problem with Mr. Karnavas's cross-examination is he's cross-examining this witness on something that is completely beyond the scope of what he was asked to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, under chapter 1, it's titled "Establishment of Herceg-Bosna political structures and their de jure foundations." When the gentleman testified on direct examination, the Prosecutor there walked him through some documents and the gentleman did comment on how there was this evolutionary process. Well, again it didn't happen in the abstract, and so I think if I'm allowed to proceed, we might -- it might become evident even to someone as closely connected to the case why I'm asking the question. And we've spent five minutes now arguing about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So, sir, do you know what happened in Ravno?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, was that a Muslim, Croat, or Serb place?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a Croat small town or village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And who were the victims in that place?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croats were the victims in this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when did the incident occur?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fall of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe October.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we've heard some testimony to the extent that at least the Sarajevo government did not do a whole lot to -- to at least give the Croats a sense of comfort that something was going to be done by the state government in protecting the Croats against these sorts of aggressive acts by the JNA or the Serbs. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the way you've phrased the question is that you've heard testimony about that and I don't know if you have or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you agree or disagree with that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That you've heard testimony about Ravno.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you disagree, sir, that the Sarajevo government did not really -- did not really respond to the needs of the Croats after the events of Ravno?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know this is something which has been argued ever since, whether or not the Sarajevo authorities did enough before and after Ravno.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did they do anything with respect to Ravno other than Izetbegovic stating, "This is not our war"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're saying that this has been a question that has been widely debated and discussed, but the question is straightforward. Did the government of Sarajevo do what was to be done after the events? You said that the question was widely debated but you as an historian, what is your point of view? Do you have a point of view? If you don't, then we'll move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as the incident in Ravno itself is concerned, I do not have a point of view on whether or not enough was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know to what extent the events in Ravno would have affected the Croatian Community in Bosnia and Herzegovina? You as an historian, that is.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't speak to their state of mind. However, I do know that they mentioned it frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, I did recount numbers of documents that were shown to Mr. Kljuic with respect to what the Croatian Community and what the Croatian leaders were talking about. One would assume that had you read those documents, you would have been able at least to form an opinion that the Croats, the Croat leadership and the Croatian people of Bosnia- Herzegovina were indeed concerned during that period of time in light of what was happening in Croatia and what looked like was going to happen in Bosnia. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course people were concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the Croats in particular, not just people. The Croats, the Croat community, the leadership they were concerned; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they say they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, are you doubting that? You say "They say they were," as if it was Alice in Wonderland?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm just trying to make it clear that I'm speaking on the basis of their documents, and I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As an historian, sir?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- what was in their mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As an historian, in light of what was happening on the ground assuming you know what was happening on the ground, do you doubt that those concerns were legitimate?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How is this related to the scope of the report? It is not. It is not, and Mr. Karnavas wants to take this witness outside the scope of the report over and over and over again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, through your interventions you are trying to undermine the work of the Defence. The Defence is trying to state its case through this witness. This case might be right or wrong. The Judges will have to rule about this at the end of this trial. But there is a case here. The case is that something happened in Ravno that had a number of consequences. What was the attitude of the Croat community? What did they do? That's the case of the Defence. Why do you want to put a spanner in the works of the Defence? Let them ask the questions, because we are wasting time here. If the witness does not answer, then the Defence will put the same questions to another witness and then you will get your feet every time again to say that this is beyond the scope of cross-examination. That's -- but that's within the scope of the questions we have to answer. We -- the indictment is not enough for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, not this witness. It's beyond the scope of what this witness was asked to do. It's like asking this witness, you wrote a report on the planet Mars and I want to ask you guess on the planet Pluto. That's what he's doing over and over again, we're talking about things beyond the scope over and over again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness gave an answer, he said he couldn't say anything about Ravno. So then he'll tell Mr. Karnavas, when he puts his questions, "I can't answer these questions." But what I'm saying, I will say also to Mr. Karnavas, if he has the statement attitude towards you. Please proceed, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in your report you conclude the HZ HB was established with the aim to become a state. And I think this we can glean from paragraph 12 of your -- of your report. But it would appear now from listening to your testimony and from the Prosecution's objections that you did not look at the establishment of the HZ HB in the context in which it was founded. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, one premise. I don't think I ever said it was founded with the establishment to be a state. If I did, you could show me that and it might be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you're not suggesting that -- hold on. Let me stop you there. So are you suggesting that it was not established, it's now your expert opinion that it was not established with the aim of becoming a state or statelet or para-state or anything of the sort within the family of statehood?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's my opinion based on everything I've seen --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that the ideal solution --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No I'm not asking you about solution. I'm asking what it was established for? Now, are you saying, under oath, as an expert for the Prosecution having worked here seven and a half years is it your expert opinion that it was established with the aim of becoming a state or statelet or para-state or anything of the sort? Is that your expert opinion; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's my opinion that it was created in order to facilitate these areas joining another state.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. That's your opinion. In other words, for them to be annexed away, to break apart?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be the ideal solution from most of the founders, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's what you're claiming their aim is. I'm trying to pin you down. I'm using very precise English language, that's your mother tongue, you're a Ph.D., kindly answer the question.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think speaking broadly about it -- broadly about everybody who was involved, I think yes the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Ideal solution would have been to have those territories join Croatia. I think everybody understood that couldn't be done immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. In light of the stated aim that you've come to conclude you did not look at the establishment of the HZ HB in the context in which it was founded; right? I'm talking about the circumstances the background, the --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- what's happening on the ground?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not strictly true. That's something I didn't go into a great deal of detail about in this particular report --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- because I didn't think --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: To what extent did you explain in your report at the state level, how the state was protecting the Croat people or even the Muslims, for that matter, during this period of time? Is that in your report; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Nothing in your report to the extent the state was able to provide Civil Defence or payments for schools, for hospitals or anything to be operating at the local level?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, its correct, I didn't mention anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact in your report you do nothing, nothing whatsoever, to look at what is happening at the state -- at the government in Sarajevo and what they're doing and how they're reacting in trying to ensure that the Croats who are coming under attack by the Serbs can be protected. You don't address that, do you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not because it wasn't my intention to discuss whether or not the foundation of Herceg-Bosna was justified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or what their motivations were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, was the HVO, the military aspect of it, was that formed legitimately under the circumstances? Yes, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's more than just one question there. First of all, the HVO --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the do you mean the HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The military -- hold on hold on. English. I'm talking about the military. Kindly listen to my question. The military aspect, when was it formed, the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO was founded 8th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what was happening in Bosnia-Herzegovina at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was right after the recognition of independence and that was towards the beginning of the fighting. The fighting actually started late March in some places.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you say fighting who is fighting whom who is being attacked, sir?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who is being attacked?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forces such as they exist, the Croat forces --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about people, man? Who is being attacked and where? You're a historian for God's sake. Tell us. Seven and a half years. Who is being attacked at that point in time that requires the HVO to be established?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: See, I wouldn't say what happened would require the HVO necessarily to be established although to get back to your earlier question --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I'll tell you who is being attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, who is being attacked?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian authorities are being attacked in north-eastern Bosnia, the authorities such as they existed in north-western Bosnia are being attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me stop you here. Were the Croats be attacked the Croats of Bosnia-Herzegovina; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in many places they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Particularly Kupres at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did -- did the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina come to their aid?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There wasn't an army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Ah, exactly. That's exactly my point. There wasn't one. Now, what about -- what about the Patriotic League? When was that established? Gee, let me think. Go on tell us, and who do you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour, these characterisations, again, I know I'm trying the President's patience. This is improper. I'm going to have to keep saying it's beyond the scope and the tone and the way he's treating the witness is objectionable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm treating the witness this way, Your Honour, because he refuses to answer questions directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's not true. Mr. Tomljanovich has answered every question when a proper question is put to him. That's completely improper and his report has nothing to do with the creation of the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has answered the questions perfectly well, but at line 15, sir, stated that there was no army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is sort of a general statement. Can you put that sort of in a temporal context? What period does it relate to? Because then the Patriotic League was set up but is this a general statement or can you put this back in the time period the relevant time period and if there was an army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, from when did it exist, from what point of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, first of all, I was making the distinction between the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina called the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and any military or paramilitary or Interior Ministry groups that may have been fighting on behalf of the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Patriotic League as far as I know and this is something I sure haven't looked at recently was being organised before fighting started. One of the leading figures was General Halilovic. I'm not sure when they were officially established although I know that the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was not officially established until later, until I believe the summer of 1992, as such. Now, in the intervening time, various local Territorial Defence units were active all over Bosnia and Herzegovina on behalf of the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When did President Izetbegovic declare a state of war, sir?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cite this in the report and off the top of my head I think that would have been sometime in June of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So we have fighting starting as early as April, April 8, 1992, and I think we can agree that there was no state armed forces at the time. You're shaking your head?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It depends what you call the state armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina as such did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Hold on the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, first of all, did that not grow out of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, partially. The Patriotic League as well as Territorial Defence units and the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And they were Muslim, were they not?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- well, if you look at the Territorial Defence units --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and these other units no, not necessarily they were not exclusively Muslim. I believe the organising core of the Patriotic League was, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What was happening in Bosnia-Herzegovina between April and, say, the time that Izetbegovic gets around to declare a state of war? What's going on? There's fighting, is there not?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's fighting all over Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And who is being attacked? General question.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, everybody's being attacked by the -- what's -- remnants of what had been the JNA and the Serb forces they're attacking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The Croats are being attacked, are they?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croats and Muslims. The Serbs are attacking the other two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in the various municipalities that ultimately became the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, could you please tell us what troops Izetbegovic, from the Sarajevo government, okay, what troops he sent to defend those areas if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact, it never happened?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say that with any certainty either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you think it might have been important for you to look at because you make the distinctions of what -- of what happened when HVO was first established and the HZ HB, the first document, and then later on where you say they take on a Presidency. We're going to get to that. That's the whole point of this whole discussion. What happened during those intervening months? Why wasn't it necessary for you, in looking at that, especially being an historian and if and it's a big if but if you wanted to put it in context to make sure that the honourable members of our Trial Chamber would know what was happening and perhaps may wish to know the motivations behind certain actions?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's a number of questions in that statement there. First of all, I'm not intending to do a general history of the conflict. Had I been doing that I would have looked at a lot of things, a much broader scope and that wasn't my intention. Now, with the rest of the questions, all I can say at the risk of being accused of being like the Nazis, I was only trying to talk about the structures and processes and not about the motivations --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We've heard --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- of the individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We've heard that defence, thank you. That's enough on that one please. Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a moment. Line 25 of page 102 and page 1 of -- line 1 of page 103 you said you were trying to talk about the structures and processes and not about the motivations. You've said that twice before. I'd like you to specify that you have not looked into the motivations, because that's the question Mr. Karnavas is putting to you at the moment. Could you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I should state it more precisely since you framed this this way and that's a good idea. I only report their intentions insofar as it's recorded in the documents by the persons doing things. I don't mean to infer from other evidence what their motivations were although if in the founding documents they say this is why we're doing this, I've reported that. But I've tried very much to keep myself sticking as closely as possible to what's in the documents themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, was it not the HDZ BiH after the establishment of the HZ HB who called on the Croat people in BiH to vote for the independent BiH at the referendum?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although that's a fairly complicated matter as well, but, yes, they did call on them to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And is it not a fact that -- that the referendum would have failed without mass Croat participation?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And is it not a fact that the HZ HB unconditionally accepted all peace plans for the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina or the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina offered by the international community --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This calls for pure speculation by this witness, it's outside the scope of his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may finish the question, Your Honour, we're not in front of the jury where we're going to taint the jury. I'm trying - - I'm learning something, Your Honour, I'm learning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas I'll object to your question at the end of it. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is it not a fact that the HZ HB unconditionally accepted all peace plans for the SRBiH offered by the international community which included for various plans for internal organisations of the country but always within the internationally recognised borders of BiH?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Objection. It calls for pure speculation by this witness. It's outside of any preparatory work he has done to answer such a questions, so calls for pure speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll lay a foundation, Your Honour. I'll lay a foundation. I'll lay a foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this question can very well be put to an historian. Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- you are an expert. You are an historian. This question, does it come within your area of expertise or beyond it as Mr. Scott says? Can an historian - is a historian able to answer that type of question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, a historian would be if he had the proper documentation at hand. Now, in that question -- I can answer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying that these documents were not available to you and that therefore you cannot answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I'm saying that I didn't take a close look at the diplomatic documentation because that's not what I'd intended to do. There are things I know in sort of a broad sense and in a rough sense in order to understand what else I'm doing, but it's nothing I've looked at very closely. I could make certain -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, Mr. Karnavas, the witness cannot answer the question, because all these diplomatic documents were not available to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm afraid he cannot, regrettably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you were shown some documents or you commented on some documents with respect to the establishment of the HZ HB, and as I understand it, you looked at the initial preamble -- preamble, and that was P 00077, and that was accompanied by to -- based, I believe, on your testimony and -- to P 00081. That was a decision on the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall the documents, not the specific exhibit numbers being which version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And in the preamble, would it not be -- and this was back on 18 November, 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the original decision was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And we talked about -- so just to recap, around 8 of April attacks begin, and Izetbegovic waits until June or July, June I think it is, to declare a state of war. I think we've agreed that to a large extent the state was incapable of providing military assistance at the very local level. The state bank wasn't functioning. Other institutions weren't functioning. Okay. Can we agree on that or do you disagree?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I could take them -- all of these assertions one by one I can tell you if I agree or disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to object to the witness speculating. I'm objecting to Mr. Tomljanovich speculating on things he hasn't researched.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll move on. I'll move on. It's obvious that the Prosecution doesn't wish this witness to testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't wish him to testify about things beyond the scope of what he's been asked to testify about, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In the preamble, this is P 00077, it says here first paragraph middle of it says: "We Croats of Bosnia-Herzegovina through our Croatian Democratic Union and through our elected government representatives in this republic have supported a sovereign Bosnia and Herzegovina, but we have always emphasised that we shall do so only until others start dividing Bosnia and Herzegovina." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And we already agreed that earlier without the Croats voting for the referendum this would not have -- right, because this --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- this follows does it not? I'm sorry I got it wrong. I apologise. You're wearing me out. You're wearing me out. Okay. But this is pretty much the Croatian attitude, is it not, that they don't want -- they want an independent Bosnia-Herzegovina. They don't want to be part of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's one aspect although the quotation you cited, what they're referring to there is that we would only support division when someone else begins to do so, which I believe is a reference to what the Serb --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- associations and municipalities are doing at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. They're saying that if the Serbs divide you know because at some point they have to figure out what Bosnia and Herzegovina is going to look like; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and in essence, that quote you read out should be understood that well, we -- Bosnia and Herzegovina might be a good thing but until such -- if somebody else is starting to break it up, that's another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Okay. You know -- now -- then it goes on then it says in the second paragraph the last part it says: "Confronted with the danger that is threatening our people and the integrity of our historic and ethnic territories and aware of our historic responsibilities in the defence of the Croat ethnic and historical -- historic territories and the Croat people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, we, the elected government representatives of the Croat people of Bosnia-Herzegovina, are founding the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna." Okay? So it would -- you would agree with me that this is -- this pretty much states their aim at this point in time, does it not?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there are a lot of terms which they leave undefined which -- such as which ethnic and historical territories, but yes, that's a broad statement of their aims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take a Croat from Herzegovina and his father, grandfather, his great great-grandfather lived in that village and given that there are a nation, one might say that at least in his or her mind that would be historic Croatian territory, would it not?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes if you're -- it's one thing if you're talking -- I think you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you mentioned Herzegovina or Herceg-Bosna in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Herzegovina that's what I --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, then there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- then you're bringing up a distinction there between Western Herzegovina which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- solidly Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. What about the Posavina? The Croats in Posavina, did they not see that -- parts of the Posavina being part of the historical, their historical heritage?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it may have been part of their historical heritage, but there they're not a majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I didn't ask you that, sir. I understand you're trying to help the Prosecutor. Just answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just trying to be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I know. Now, there was a decision that followed that preamble; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And we looked at Article 7 and I want to read this it's short and gun I want to point out 18 November, 1991, Article 7: "The supreme authority of the community shall be the Presidency comprising the most senior representatives of the Croatian people in the municipal authority or presidents of the Croatian Democratic Union municipal boards." Then it goes on to say: "The Presidency shall elect the president, two deputy presidents and the secretary." Now, my question is at this point in time 18 November, 1991, at least when -- when it's being established, this Presidency is not a legislative body, is it?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm asking you based on this document, sir. It's in English. You told us you're able to read certain documents?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is there -- does this -- does this state, Article 7, what the functions are of the Presidency, what it will do?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not having it in front of me, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. It's P -- it's -- if I could have the usher's assistance we can get this on the ELMO and this is a document that you made reference, a document that the Prosecution questioned you on, a document that I assume you have read and are familiar with. Article 7. This is the initial one. Okay?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At that point in time. Now, is there any dilemma as to what functions concretely the Presidency, which is the supreme authority, will have?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to this Article it's just very vague. It just says supreme authority without specifying exactly what that means.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly. That's my point. So at this point in time, the Presidency is not a legislative body, is it? Or is it?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that depends on how you look at it. If you look at the founding of the HVO in April as an act of legislation, then it would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Hold on. Hold on. The HVO was what?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When it was founded in April and we already talked about what was happening; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO was the -- I believe it's the supreme body -- I forget the exact wording, but it's -- the wording was in the 8th of April decision. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was it a civilian authority, sir the HVO back in April? Is that what we're talking about, a civilian authority?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe if you look at the -- if you look at the decision, it would say that it's both for the defence and executive organ as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although the details of that aren't spelled out until May 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Getting back to this Article 7, can you tell us with any degree of certainty, legal or otherwise, whether at this point in time the Presidency is a legislative body?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as it did create and act on the 8th of April and did create another body, in that sense, you can say that's legislative. You can say the founding of the HVO was a legislative, and that body only exists because of this decision. Now, if you don't think that's legislation, then maybe not, but I'd say yes based on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you consult anybody, sir, in order to give this upon or are you just rattling off whatever comes to the top of your head?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this particular question hadn't been posed to me until just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, they do have lawyers at the Office of the Prosecution, do they not, that speak B/C/S and could assist you in actually interpreting documents such as this, such as the constitution, such as the All People's Defence, such as the law on the -- the state law on administration and all those sorts of things they have she is sorts of expert services at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sure if we'd done that, Your Honour, Mr. Karnavas would be objecting to interfering with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think at this point in time any interference with this witness would be a welcome relief. Let me move or not to the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now -- now, after -- after this date, did you by any chance consult the statement of principles of the 18th of March of 1992? You we brought this up when Mr. Kljuic was here 1D 00389. Okay. Did you look at this? This is part of the negotiating documents that the international community was proposing. And if we were to accept the editor's note, it says, "The following statements of principles were agreed upon by the leadership of the three sides of the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina in March 1992. However, it was subsequently repudiated by the Bosnian Presidency." Okay. Did you look at that document by any chance?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not exactly sure what the document is but I believe that this is something which I did not look at specifically for this report because I wasn't intending on dealing with the diplomatic events in that detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I see. And just -- just as an aside since you -- there was this dilemma earlier about nationalities versus ethnicities, just to put it right, had you read this document even if you had disagreed with your mentor Ivo Banac, which seems you may have some disagreement with, it says here that: "Sovereignty reside in the citizens of Muslims Serbs and Croat nations, in other nations and nationalities who realise it through their civic participation in the constituent units in the central organs of the republic." So at least if we are to accept this document, it appears that there is no dilemma among the parties that we're dealing with constituent nations and not ethnicities; right?Well, actually, they're making a distinction here and they're using a term of art in the B/C/S that's worth mentioning, because they're talking about nations and nationalities, and nations in that sense would be -- Q. Yes.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the Croats, the Muslims, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the Serbs --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- who are enfranchised in the former Yugoslavia. Now, nationalities would be those groups like Hungarians, Italians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Roma whatever?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: And people who don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just to make sure we get it absolutely right, in Croatia a large number of Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with 12, 13 per cent of the population at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay just help me out here were they a nation or were an ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were a nation --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Under the then constitution?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a constitutional concept, they were a nation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That would --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're use the terms in the sense that the former Yugoslav constitutional law did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So hold on I want to make sure I got this right. Heart be still. Are you suggesting that in the former Yugoslavia, okay, when it was altogether under that constitution the Serbs that lived in Croatia were recognised as a nation of that republic as opposed to an ethnic group? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe they did and I think that the removal of their constitutive status is what they were upset about in the 1990s or one of the things they were upset about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Were they not considered a national minority?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in you're using the terms they way they did in communist Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There is a difference between a national minority and a nation because -- well, let me ask you this: In Bosnia-Herzegovina you only had 17.5 per cent who were Croat. Where I come from, which is the United States, that might be a minority. Okay? Maybe a national minority. Okay? Versus -- now are you suggesting that there is no difference between the way the Croats were in -- in Bosnia-Herzegovina as a nation and the Serbs as they were in -- in Croatia? In other words, are you -- do you not see the -- do you not make a distinction between --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were both.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Between --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Between nation and minority, national minority? Do you not make the distinction?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, whether or not I make the distinction you could define these terms any way you like, except --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is there a distinction in the legal instruments which you have indicated you have read?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the former Yugoslav system and constitution, the constitutive nations of the then Yugoslavia were those countries who were primarily based within that country and those were nations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're given.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, that's enough. That's enough. I asked you a concrete question let me move on. Okay. Now -- now after this -- this -- this date we talked about, this document was March 1992. Now, in April 26, 1992, let me show you what has been marked as 1D 005 -- 525. 1D 00525 dated April 26, 1992. It has Herceg-Bosna on top of it. You did indicate that you looked at relevant documents. Have you seen this document, sir? Yes, no, I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall seeing this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you -- do you think, just by looking at it, given that it's generated by Herceg-Bosna signed by Mate Boban and the relevant date that it might be within the scope of your limited mandate?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily. I'd have to give it a good look to see, but in general I didn't look at every document. I made a point of not looking at every document concerning the peace negotiations because that would be a large task in and of itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, don't you think it might have been important here in light of the relevant date to see what Mate Boban's intent was, what he was -- since he was the president of the community of Herceg-Bosna? Did you not think that might be relevant?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I think you mean his stated intent. And secondly it may be relevant but then again probably not because I didn't -- there's a lot of documents concerning the peace negotiations and as I said, that would be taking me too far afield.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well paragraph -- let's look at paragraph 3 for instance and maybe you can tell me if this is relevant or not. It says, "Still convinced that the principles of the negotiations under the patronage of the European Community are the only possible way for the establishing -- for the establishing of the government of the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that the war still can be stopped, it is necessary to apply at once some of the agreed principles of the future constitutional arrangements of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Now, in reading that, at least does -- can we not glean from this his stated position, that is Mate Boban's position, to work within the negotiated process of the European Community? Doesn't that say that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And he's writing, by the way, to Mr. Cutileiro; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Serious individual?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Part of the negotiating process at the time?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Trying to find a solution in all this madness to try and stop the war?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Alija Izetbegovic; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he's there and he's here as the president of his own political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Are you doubting that he was not the president of that political party which was for the most part you know representing most of the Muslims in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And of course he's sending it also to Karadzic who was the head of the Serb party, the SDS; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then it goes on to say: "Therefore we suggest that instead of disintegrated and I am legal authorities, immediately a ministry council of Bosnia and Herzegovina should be mandated consisting of nine members (a party of the three people) as the European Community has proposed, being the only authority of temporary governing Bosnia and Herzegovina." So here do we not see -- help me out here, sir. Do we not see the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna proposing this nine-person committee under the auspices of the European Community to be the only legal authority, including authority over the Croatian Community? Is he not proposing that? Here, April 26, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that appears to be what he's proposing with one minor difference. You read in the parenthetical phrase a party, and it's a parity of the three, meaning that each nation would get a third of the representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. The print is rather small I appreciate that correction. The gist of it is April 26 again I hate to go back on this chronology maybe many' stuck in context and background, no knows, but we've got April 8. We talked about the attacks begin, and here we are and then we have the statement of principles, March 18, okay. Talking about three peoples organised. Here April 26, right, and you have Boban suggesting that there be an authority for the entire country, is he not?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he's saying here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in your report, and I hate to go back to it again. In your report, you don't show us anything, anything of the events anything historical we can grab latch on to that would give us some indication of what is happening in Bosnia and Herzegovina during this very critical period of time that would lead someone like Mate Boban to suggest that the European Community in essence run the country. Can I ask a question: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this is getting into the day-to-day diplomatic manoeuvring at that time which is something I thought was outside of the scope of what I should be doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But then -- but then I notice that you did not hesitate, you did not flinch, in fact, in commenting about the decision that followed, which was I think 3 July, 1992, on the establishment of the Croatian Community; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So in other words, in your report and in your testimony when you gave evidence for the Prosecution, you want to show this transition as to what they establish first and so on, and then you go on to 3 July, and we can see that it's -- that the HZ HB is taking on a different, you know, form, all right? But you see no reason to see whether there is a cause and effect, a ying and a yang. You see no reason as if nothing was happening; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think this is a good case of explaining what I did cite and what I didn't. Now, everything that's enacted on the 3rd July 1992 falls very directly within what it was I was trying to do. This is the people involved in Herceg-Bosna themselves setting up their own institutions. Going into the diplomatic background of what all else is going on is something which I thought other witnesses would deal with; in particular, live witnesses who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Being an historian, sir, having spent seven and a half years, almost as much as you did spending on your Ph.D. dissertation, would it be fair to say that at this point in time you would be able to tell us what exactly occurred during this period of time in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in broad sense, not exactly what happened throughout that entire period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say in a general sense, then, that the events deteriorated -- in Bosnia-Herzegovina, deteriorated, say, from 8 April till later on? Did they deteriorate?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, things were clearly very bad all through the spring and summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so -- and would it be fair to say when I say deteriorate, I'm not just saying militarily, but when Sarajevo came under siege would it be fair to say and I don't think you need to be an economist or a military or constitutional expert, but would it be fair to say that the state organs, the state government was providing fewer and fewer services for the entire country?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I would say fewer and fewer but not as much as anyone would like at the time but fewer our fewer I'm not sure of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was Sarajevo under siege?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this period, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And is it your opinion that Sarajevo was able to provide water, electricity outside of Sarajevo to the various municipalities?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the Sarajevo authorities?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah, the Sarajevo authorities, the government. You know --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. In same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not saying --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some places, they had water and history, and in others they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: To what extent was the Sarajevo government functioning?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a hard thing to quantify.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can talk about what they did and did not do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that's gets a long way out of what I was planning to talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Fair to say, though because I don't want to leave the point unsaid, fair to say that throughout this period when we just looked at these documents starting with April -- April 8th, the situation, particularly with respect to civil governance and the ability of the state to provide for its citizens at the very local level had deteriorated significantly?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That depends on what you're talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and from what period you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I can tell you what I mean about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Tell me what parts the Sarajevo government was able to provide all of its services to, including starts be with Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: All services that's different. Now I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Tuzla, pick Tuzla which was a multi-ethnic community. Pick Tuzla. How much -- you know and -- because you must have looked at those documents. What was the state government able to provide for Tuzla? If you don't know say you don't know. We have an objection now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I object to speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There is over and over again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The Court doesn't understand apparently the issue of the scope, so I'm trying not to get on my feet again but all this is speculation all this is beyond the scope and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers not speak at the same time, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It's of course up to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The gentleman said, Your Honour, that it all depends. I gave him two examples one is Tuzla; the other one is Bihac. Now, he either knows or he don't know. If he don't know I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Without going into speculation, the Defence is talking about Tuzla and Bihac. Are you in a position to answer the question without any speculation? Give us an answer if you're certain of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I can say about Tuzla and Bihac is that they were well organised enough to maintain the defence of those areas and hang on to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. That's not the question. Please do not eat up my time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I asked you specifically: What services was the state able to provide to them? So just answer that very narrow scope.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, and this was part of the answer: Defence. They did provide defence and that defence was successful ultimately. Now, as far as utility-type services that, you know, when the water was on, when the electricity was on how well the municipal governments were functioning that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, very well. We'll cover that with others. I want -- I don't have enough time so I'm going to have to skip around a little bit. Dealing with the ultimatum of January 15, 1993. Now, as I understand your testimony on direct, I just want to make sure that I -- I caught it right. You were not aware of any events occurring in Gornji Vakuf prior to this particular incident, January 15 -- this particular ultimatum of January 15, 1993. Am I correct on that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately prior, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So are you suggesting here, sir, that you don't know whether something happened or is it your expert opinion, being a historian and having read and spent all this time in the archives, that nothing in fact did occur in Gornji Vakuf prior to the 15th? And I state this because the Prosecution is alleging that it was that ultimatum that precipitated all of this fighting. So there's a point to this question. And --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So do you know or you don't know? If you don't know --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware in a very general sense that there was fighting I believe going as far as Gornji Vakuf municipality after the events in Prozor in October.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. What about in January, sir, in January?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, that specifically Gornji Vakuf I couldn't tell you about the first half of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And would it surprise you if I were to tell you that incidents were occurring and as a historian, one cannot look at this ultimatum as precipitating something if something is already happening; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily because what you're doing there is you're reducing everything that happens because of the ultimatum of the 15th of January simply to Gornji Vakuf municipality. And things happened elsewhere as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That was decision that was issued, was there not, in January 15th?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That decision -- now, that's the one we're talking about this ultimatum; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're also talking about the decision which Mr. Prlic signed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, incidentally, did you ever as a -- you know, as a historian or as an expert for the Prosecution or just out of curiosity, did you ever look at to see how many troops and which brigades would have been subordinated -- HVO, HVO brigades or troops would have been subordinated to the ABiH? Because I think this was an issue that Judge Trechsel had asked at one point in time. So did you ever bother to say -- to look at it or was this sort of a Trojan horse?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I know which areas it is they're talking about where there are concentrations of HVO troops in those areas. Now, with actual numbers, I couldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Don't you think it might have been relevant to see what exactly -- because we're talking about this ultimatum. The Prosecution is alleging that this caused all these events and what have you. You have written about the ultimatum of the 15th and now us it's clear that your he not aware that immediately before the 15th, days and weeks, there was -- there was ongoing fighting and what have you. Now, is there a particular reason why you did not look to see and try to make some kind of comparison because after all, troops are being -- Croatian troops are being asked to subordinate themselves under the ABiH. This is very critical.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, no. Well, two things. First of all that is a question I asked myself and I can give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you ever answer it?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The areas in which you're talking about mainly where there's still a fair number of HVO troops there's a small HVO contingent in Tuzla. There's Zepce. There's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Zenica?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not -- Kakanj and Vares -- Kakanj and Vares which are large numbers of HVO troops at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one unit in western Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would it your surprise you, sir, we're talking about my calculations and we hope to establish this but at my calculation we're talking approximately 18.000 troops? Would that surprise you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's -- I'd be surprised if it was that high.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it was in the thousands but not 18.000 because that's just off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and I take it this didn't come up -- we produced this document so I don't expect you to have -- maybe you did see it but there was one document that we were able to show a handwritten document, it's 1D 00820. It's a handwritten document or letter or note that was sent by Mr. Boban where he's ordering, he's ordering the HVO, the civilian authority, to convene a special meeting and to change item 5 of this decision. Did you by any chance see this document?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure which document you're talking about not being able to look at it or even knowing the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But even from this -- well, the date is January 20th. I don't know if we have it up on the ELMO yet or the -- the e-court. It's 1D 00820, and I can provide you with a hard copy if you like to save time but it says here in reference to your decision number 01-1-31/93, "… and after the discussion with the co-chairmen of the Geneva conference on Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mr. Vance, and Lord Owen, I'm ordering you to convene a special meeting during the day and change item 5 in a way to set up a deadline for the implementation of the decision." Now, based on your knowledge, was Boban in a capacity to issue such an order de jure, de facto, de Boban, whatever?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he certainly was the person present at the peace talks and would have been the one to tell them and also yes, constitutionally, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, constitutionally -- what constitution are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, hold on a second. Now that I think about it --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Uh-huh. uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I'm not entirely sure if the existing laws or ordinances of Herceg-Bosna would have allowed him to do this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: January 20th, 1993 who is the Supreme Commander of the HVO, of the military?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the armed forces, it would be Boban.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And this decision does it not relate to subordination of units?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not, although off the top of my head, I'm not sure what item 5 is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, item 5 had to do with -- well, it's -- well, again this is the -- it's your document. It's P 011346 but it has to do with subordination. That's what it has to do and the time frame. That's what it has to do with, the time frame itself.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So is Boban -- and let me ask you this by the way before you answer that question perhaps it might help you out would it surprise you thereafter that there is a decision that is rendered by the HVO making some references which in fact changes item 5, and this is 1D 00821. So if we put two and two together -- this would be -- yeah. So if we put two and two together, it would appear that Boban orders the HVO authorities comply and issue a decision to change item 5. Now, let me ask you, sir, did you see this by any chance?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This particular document I've never seen before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That's 1D 00821, the decision. Have you seen the decision that's signed by Dr. Jadranko Prlic as president of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure. I don't think so but not seeing the document I'm not sure if it's familiar or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I suspect not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You suspect that you hadn't seen it?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suspect not but I'm not absolutely positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And -- now do you want to take a -- do you want to answer the question whether you know for a fact -- don't speculate, don't assume, do you know whether Boban at this particular period in time based on the existing legislation was legally capable of issuing such an order, in other words, was the order legal in the sense, to the HVO, the civilian authority?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: – instance, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That's -- thank you for that frank answer that you don't know. Now -- all right. Now, it begs the question how is it you don't know? Because one the very first questions I asked if not the very -- the first question is what are you an expert in? We know you're an expert on 19th century history in relation to Croatia. We also know what you're not: Constitutional expert, you know financing expert, economics, military and so on and so forth, but you said that you spent a lot of time in this area, and you were an expert in a sense on the establishment and the functionings of the HZ HB, HR HB, and I'm asking you now, since you're the expert, how you can stand here in front of our honourable members and say you cannot say to any degree of certainty, legal or otherwise, whether Boban at that point in time, could issue a legal order of such nature?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
