utterances.text: Well, when I say that I mean legal within the system of laws and ordinances they created for Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly, that's what I'm talking about. So that means that you would have to look at the legal instruments. So are you suggesting at this point in time Boban was acting de facto as the leader and not de jure?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if this document is indeed genuine, he is acting de facto and de facto giving an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But that don't take a genius to figure out because we have a signature so actually he did it. Now the question is de jure. Yes, no, I don't know?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depends on how you read the founding documents. I can only point you to the founding documents and you can make arguments that he's allowed to do it and not allowed to do it and -- with an order like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. By the way did you look at and I don't have time, but did you look at any of the other documents that went back and forth such as meetings of the meeting -- minutes of the meetings that -- that took place between the 15th and the 20th generated by Mr. Prlic in his capacity or at meetings where the HVO civilian authorities met? Did you look at any of that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I looked at everything I could find. Now, there's a lot of records which are missing and the record is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- incomplete so I probably looked at something from that period but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I very well may not have seen anything from that period as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I was go to ask you to assume something but I think that would be -- that would be asking too much. Incidentally on the establishment of the HR HB, okay? I think we pretty much established the fact that you didn't look at anything -- didn't put anything into context when the HZ HB was established. Can we assume, can we assume that it was the same thing with the establishment of the HR HB? In other words, you didn't take anything into context? You didn't look at the historical events, the peace proposals such as the Owen- Stoltenberg or Stoltenberg-Owen plan? You didn't look at any of that not to mention what's happening on the ground the events? You didn't -- you didn't -- that's not into your -- in your report is it?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well those are two different things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did look at those things and am familiar with those things but I did not think it was appropriate to put a lot of diplomatic background into the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So again, if we look at the report we don't know cause and effect if there is such a thing if something caused the effect, something cause the HZ HB to become HR HB such as you know maybe because of the negotiations that were going on?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe I did mention that because that was their -- they state, I believe in the foundation of the HR HB, they state they're doing this and at least what they can be in conjunction with the direction the negotiations are taking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Of the peace proposals?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what was being proposed at the time, the Stoltenberg-Owen plan, you would have you would have three republics within Bosnia- Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was supposed to be a union of three republics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: A union of three republics. And so -- and that would -- fine. I'll leave it at that. I'll leave it at that. With -- there was some testimony with respect to Vares and the evacuation of Vares, okay? And perhaps we can go through this real quickly. I'm uncertain here. Was something happening to the Croats up there which caused them to want to leave or have to leave or is it your opinion that it was the Croatian Community or the Croat leaders that were actually trying to ethnically cleanse their own people? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I can have a second just to give you a full answer for this. By the sum of 1993 there were several real, very real and pressing reasons for people in Kakanj to be afraid and those are persons who fled to Vares. And then from Vares elsewhere so there are reasons, on the one hand, yes, reasons for people good reasons for people to have wanted to flee those areas at that time. Now on the other hand I never said they were ethnically cleansing their own people in those words. What I did mention was there's a sort of ambiguity about it where the HVO leaders say on the one hand it's a same this is happening but on the other hand this gives us a chance to round off our territories.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That's your -- that's your interpretation.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well all right. If I can show you a document, I have a series of four documents and I think we with wrap this up. 4D 00022. And this is -- while it's being pulled up this is dated 2 July, 1993. And I'm going to start reading into the record at the bottom of the page it says: "In view of the fact that the population of Vares municipality is in a desperate situation due to the huge influx of displaced persons who are still arriving from Kakanj area day after day, we are forced to appeal to you," and so on and so forth. So that's what you were talking about; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And at least if we look at the date, and we look at who is the author and we look at what is being described, it would appear that they do have a humanitarian crisis looming in the air as it were.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A large number of refugees who weren't able to go anywhere from Kakanj went into Vares which was already in a very difficult situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, just to put it into historical context, if we look at 4D 00023. This document is dated 9 July, 1993, and this is by the commander of the brigade Emil Harah, and it states here: "As you already know, after the area of the Kakanj municipality in the army of BiH side has been occupied and after approximately 15.000 Croats had been expelled in our area of responsibility, the municipality of the HVO Vares found itself in an extremely difficult existential and war conditions, in extremely difficult existential and war conditions," and it goes on. You don't dispute that do you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm sure it was difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we can look at another document. P 02283. And this is from -- this is a Prosecution document dated the 11th of May, and this is from General -- Colonel Blaskic. He was a colonel at the time. He was a commander. You're aware of him; right?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And in this letter, if we just -- you know, he talks about the evacuation being carried out and is giving his reasons why it has to be carried out and where.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me just -- let me --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- help you out here, because at the very end, I want to flip to the end because I'm running out of time unless you want me to cross-examine you tomorrow, which I'll be happy to do so for a couple of hours, it says: "Send a political representative to the territories from where the evacuation is to be carried out." And then it goes on and it ends with, "...in ten days, everything might be too late and everything can turn into a huge tragedy of more than 10.000 Croats of Central Bosnia and it started already with the suffering of Croats in Zenica and Konjic." All right, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay I don't want to go through -- there is one last document and this is P 034113, and this is the one from Jadranko Prlic and that's 13 July, 1993. I think we looked at it already. I don't want to look at it, but would it be fair to say, sir, that if, if we are interested in trying to determine what is motivating the HVO HZ HB, on 13 July, 1993, in submitting this letter, would we not, at least if we want to be fair and balanced, would we not have to look at all of these other documents which show that as early as May there was a problem in Vares and that problem was not the Croats trying to ethnically cleanse their own people but, rather, get them out of harm's way because of the looming catastrophe?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes and no. Actually, this document here from May I don't believe mentions Vares or Kakanj in particular. As a matter of fact, it's unclear exactly what territory I think they're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, none of these documents that I showed you were put into your report, were they?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the context -- well, the context in which I put these documents in, is that in your report?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The argumentation you made was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the argumentation is based on if we look at the chronology of the events. That's not in your report, is it?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document we're looking at right now I believe was in my report, this last one you've showed me from Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Very well. With that, Mr. President, in keeping with our pressing time schedule, although I would like to cross-examine for a few more hours tomorrow, I will conclude -- this will conclude my cross-examination. I know it was very trying for the Trial Chamber, and -- but I tried --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You won't [as interpreted] have any more hours tomorrow. We decided that there would be a maximum of two additional hours tomorrow. Therefore, tomorrow you will have two hours max and then we'll stop. And Ms. Nozica will have -- and my fellow Judge tells me that we have to take into account the 20 minutes allocated to Ms. Nozica. Therefore, there will be an additional two hours max for the completion of the testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I will take that under advisement and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, because apparently there was a mistake in the translation. Are you requiring or do you want additional time tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not demanding additional time, Mr. President. If offered, I would take it, but in my opinion I don't think it's necessary for me to continue to cross-examine this particular expert, such as he is. I think my cross-examination can rest at this point in time, though I appreciate the Court -- the Court's willingness to give me additional time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Very well. Very well. Then tomorrow Ms. Nozica will have 20 minutes. It's five past 7.00. We will reconvene tomorrow at a quarter past 2.00. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 19th day of September, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.05 p.m.,
